claims.text: The starting catalyst is a near-equiatomic, multi-principal-element alloy.
The starting catalyst has a homogeneous bulk composition.
The starting catalyst has no pronounced surface segregation.
Oxidative pre-treatment annealing will selectively segregate copper to the catalyst surface.
Oxidation of the surface-segregated copper will form a Cu-rich oxide overlayer or nanoclusters.
The Cu-rich oxide phase will catalyze low-temperature oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons in a manner analogous to Cu–Ni catalysts.
The Cu-rich surface phase will improve resistance to poisoning by H2O and NO in a manner analogous to Pd–Cu and Pt–Cu catalysts.
Stabilizing the surface composition will mitigate catalyst degradation during prolonged thermal cycling.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the oxidatively pre-treated catalyst will have a lower light-off temperature.
The treated catalyst will activate below 150 °C.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will retain higher CO and hydrocarbon conversion in the presence of H2O and NO.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will retain activity better after accelerated aging intended to mimic a full vehicle lifetime.
The predicted improvements are restricted to transient automotive exhaust operation below 150 °C and to the specified accelerated-aging regime.
The accelerated thermal-cycling and mileage-related degradation protocol realistically simulates a full vehicle lifetime.
